source.version: Author accepted manuscript for Computers & Education, dated March 9th, 2024. PDF p. 1 explicitly says it is not the copy of record and supplies final-article DOI 10.1016/j.compedu.2024.105031. This extraction uses the manuscript on file, not the publisher version.
source.supplement_used: Appendix 1: Evaluation Matrix for a Product Improvement Task, included in the same PDF on p. 40. No separate supplement is on file for c123.

studies.label: Lab experiment: Product Improvement Task with vs. without ChatGPT
studies.cluster_se_treatment: No session clustering is reported. Students were individually randomized before the experiment, but the two conditions ran in separate sessions. The t-tests and ANCOVAs treat participants as independent (PDF pp. 10 and 16).

counts_source.quote: The control group for the present study contained 68 university students and the experimental group contained 77 participants

arms.name: Experimental (ChatGPT)
arms.description: Solved the PIT with ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus) open in a second browser tab after a brief introduction with example prompts and responses. This arm also answered additional self-efficacy items about using ChatGPT (PDF pp. 10 and 13).

arms.name: Control (no ChatGPT)
arms.description: Solved the same PIT with only the experimental-task browser tab open and no ChatGPT. Both arms could access additional browser tools, but no participant did so (PDF p. 10).

studies.task: Generate three original and useful improvements to a stuffed bunny to help Mattel achieve higher sales than the Lego Group (PDF pp. 12-13).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 10, Experimental Procedure; no model release year is stated.

preregistration.where: Open Science Framework, https://osf.io/q6wtu (PDF p. 9). The manuscript says the design and hypotheses were preregistered; the registration itself was not examined.

studies.shared_sample: Per forms/c123.json, sample_overlap: Urban et al. (2025), Prompting for creative problem-solving: A process-mining study, Learning and Instruction 99, 102156 (c594), reuses the 77 experimental-arm participants and their PIT ratings. Its preprint states the overlap on p. 9. This overlap is supplied by the reconciled form; the c123 manuscript does not identify the later paper.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two experts independently rated answers in randomized order, blind to condition. Five-point scale from worst to best; quality is alignment with the goals of improving the bunny and increasing sales. See PDF p. 13 and Appendix 1, PDF p. 40. The paper does not explain how PIT ratings and the three proposed solutions were combined into a participant score.

estimates.outcome: Originality: randomized group-by-task interaction from UUT baseline to PIT
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Expert-rated originality across the unassisted Unusual Uses Task baseline and the subsequent Product Improvement Task. Both original scales run from one to five; Figure 1 displays z-scores. The UUT score is the mean of two blinded expert judgments (PDF p. 12); PIT scoring and its unresolved aggregation are described on PDF p. 13. The figure does not print numerical z-score means or confidence limits.

estimates.notes: Included as the reported full-sample randomized contrast in change from baseline to the experimental task, not as a participant-subgroup or prior-experience moderation result. This is a parallel-group experiment with repeated task measurements, not a randomized-order crossover: everybody completed the unassisted UUT first, and only the experimental group then used ChatGPT on the PIT. within_person is therefore null. The task changes as well as AI availability; this does not isolate within-person AI effects on a constant task. The preceding Results paragraph states that hypothesis tests use prior ChatGPT experience as a covariate, but no complete model specification for this interaction is printed. Figure 1 labels its error bars as 95% CI, without numerical limits; no values were read off the graph. No change means, change SDs, SEs, or difference are printed. Shares the same sample and endpoint with the other originality records.

open_items: The source prints arm sizes but no combined analyzed total. Study n_analyzed and estimate n_total are null rather than computed by summing the arms. The reconciled screening form gives a combined total, but it is not printed in this manuscript.

The paper states individual random assignment before the experiment and no exclusions, but does not print counts at assignment, the randomization mechanism, or the number of assigned volunteers who did not attend. Randomized counts remain null.

PIT score construction is incomplete: the paper does not identify the PIT raters or explain how their ratings and the three solutions become one participant score. The inferential analyses support participant-level coding, but the aggregation procedure remains unspecified.
The arms ran in separate sessions with at most five people per session. Session counts and scheduling are unreported; no adjustment for session clustering is described.
The manuscript names no primary outcome or ranking among the preregistered H1 dimensions. The OSF registration was not examined, so preregistered_primary is not_stated.
No model release year is printed. The tool name is retained verbatim from the Methods, and ai_tool.year is null.
The manuscript does not specify the standardizer for its reported d values. The unadjusted records retain the printed participant-level arm SDs.
Adjusted ANCOVA arm means, differences, SEs, coefficients, and confidence limits are not printed. The group-by-task analysis likewise lacks change summaries and a complete model specification.
Figure 1 presents z-score means and confidence bars without numerical labels. No values were digitized or inferred from the graph.
The journal version of record is not the PDF on file; the extraction is limited to the accepted manuscript and its included appendix.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-10; extractor B, independent reconciliation pending. All markdown lines were read through the end of Appendix 1. PDF tables, all figures, and the appendix were inspected before the design and methods; every numerical estimate was transcribed from pymupdf text on the cited PDF page. PDF page numbers and printed page numbers agree. The three Table 2 outcome rows contain arm means, SDs, t-tests, p bounds, and d; the H1 text contains three adjusted condition F-tests, p bounds, and partial eta squared; the Figure 1 paragraph contains the full-sample originality group-by-task F-test, p-value, and partial eta squared. These specifications share one randomized sample and must not be pooled as independent studies. Table 2 numbers are unadjusted and are not presented as adjusted ANCOVA means. Source quotations preserve the printed decimal precision, including trailing zeros. No effects, totals, SEs, or intervals were calculated. Country is inferred from the laboratory being at the first author’s institution (PDF p. 9) and that institution’s Prague, Czech Republic affiliation (PDF p. 1), consistent with the reconciled form. Hypothesis H1 covers all three PIT dimensions but does not designate a primary outcome. Under the codebook hierarchy, originality is the preferred construct; among its direct endpoint specifications, the paper identifies ANCOVA as its main hypothesis-testing analysis, while the unadjusted record preserves the arm statistics for standardization. There is no diversity outcome or output produced after AI was removed; the unassisted UUT occurred before treatment.
